response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT e.ordersmark, o.timespan, AVG(e.fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.timespan), scored AS (SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, AVG(avg_fill) OVER (PARTITION BY timespan) AS tif_avg, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY timespan ORDER BY avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS fill_rank FROM per_order) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, avg_fill - tif_avg AS above_tif_avg, fill_rank FROM scored WHERE avg_fill > tif_avg AND fill_rank <= 3 ORDER BY timespan, fill_rank, ordersmark

assumptions.assumption: The time-in-force average fill is the mean of the per-order average fills across the matched orders in that time in force. Each order counts once, and orders whose fillcount values are all null are ignored.
Rank is computed among all matched orders in the time in force, before filtering to those above the average. Orders with a null average rank last.
Orders with no matching executions do not appear. Orders with a null timespan form their own group.

alternatives.interpretation: The time-in-force average fill is the mean of fillcount over all individual executions in that time in force, so orders with more executions weigh more.
alternatives.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT e.ordersmark, o.timespan, e.fillcount FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault), per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, timespan, AVG(fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM j GROUP BY ordersmark, timespan), tif AS (SELECT timespan, AVG(fillcount) AS tif_avg FROM j GROUP BY timespan), scored AS (SELECT p.ordersmark, p.timespan, p.avg_fill, t.tif_avg, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.timespan ORDER BY p.avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS fill_rank FROM per_order p JOIN tif t ON t.timespan IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p.timespan) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, avg_fill - tif_avg AS above_tif_avg, fill_rank FROM scored WHERE avg_fill > tif_avg AND fill_rank <= 3 ORDER BY timespan, fill_rank, ordersmark
